key_insight: Distill the utility judgments of an LLM re-ranker into dense vector embeddings so retrieval behaves like LLM re-ranking but runs at dense-search speeds, combining high utility with practical efficiency.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between fast but imprecise dense similarity search and slow but higher-utility LLM re-ranking — mitigating compute cost and noisy perplexity-based signals while improving retrieval relevance for RAG systems.
method: Use an LLM re-ranker as a teacher to produce utility scores / pairwise preferences over document candidates.
Train a dense encoder (student) via utility-aware distillation so embedding similarities reflect the LLM's utility judgments (contrastive/regression distillation loss).
Deploy the trained embeddings for fast nearest-neighbor retrieval, reducing dependence on expensive reranking while preserving LLM-aligned relevance.
impact: Allows practitioners to get LLM-quality retrieval relevance at dense-search latency and cost, improving downstream RAG fidelity and scalability without continuous expensive re-ranking.
